entries.english: Civil disputes among residents of Aub and its surroundings, and Jewish affairs, 1570–1629. The volume includes: a dispute between Ottilia Meder zu Adelhofen and her son-in-law Michael Nickel zu Holzhausen, including an exchange of his farm for one belonging to Leonhard Mohn zu Simmershofen (1605–1607); the Lords von Rosenberg’s undated complaint to the Imperial Chamber Court against Bischof Julius zu Würzburgs ban on trade with Jews; Christoph Hepel of Hemmersheim’s debt statement (1629); Michael Rauch’s insult complaint against Hans Beyer, both of Aub (1604); misconduct by the tower guard and gatekeepers at Aub (1618); the wounding of miller Leonhard Sulleder by Kilian Scheffner of Aub (1615); the Kannegießer Barthel Zieg’s marital disputes and mismanagement of his household (1593–1594); an insult dispute between Isaak of Aub and Lazarus of Hüttenheim (1599); Isaak’s transfer by an imperial commission in Mainz for investigation of alleged Jewish crimes (1601, 1607); miscellaneous matters (1570–1598 and 1615–1629); and a summons issued by the Mergentheim court against Isaak for claiming jurisdiction over Mayer of Mergentheim (1615). One volume.
